editorial_contributions.text:
The Cayley-Dickson algebras considered here are the real (not necessarily associative) algebras in the sequence obtained starting with \(A_0={\mathbb R}\), by means of the Cayley-Dickson doubling process: \(A_{n+1}=A_n\times A_n\) with multiplication \((a,b)(c,d)=(ac-\bar db,da+b\bar c)\) and involution \(\overline{(a,b)}=(\bar a,-b)\). The first algebras in the sequence are the familiar algebras of the real, complex, quaternion and octonion numbers. These are all division algebras. 

The late \textit{G. Moreno} [Bol. Soc. Mat. Mex. 4, No. 3, 13--28 (1998; Zbl 1006.17005)] studied the zero divisors in \(A_n\) for \(n\geq 4\). The paper under review continues this research. The main results assert that for any \(x\in A_n\), \(\text{ann}(x)=\{y\in A_n: xy=0\}\) \((=\{y\in A_n: yx=0\})\) is a subspace whose dimension \(d\) is a multiple of \(4\) with \(0\leq d\leq 2^n-4n+4\), and that for any such \(d\) there is an element \(x\in A_n\) with \(\dim \text{ann}(x)=d\). Moreover, the elements whose annihilators have the largest possible dimension (\(2^n-4n+4\)) are described.
